instruction: Enable the 'Send a Do Not Track request' option in Chrome's privacy and security settings.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y
cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"session":{"restore_on_startup":4, "startup_urls":["http://funbrain.com/"]}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to Chrome Settings > On start-up, found funbrain.com configured as startup page, clicked context menu > Remove, resulting in 'Open the New Tab page' being selected. Evaluator returned 0 despite UI showing correct state.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to Settings, find specific settings sections, interact with toggles and UI controls
metadata.failure_analysis: Model appeared to complete the original task but evaluator returned 0.0. Model demonstrated strong Chrome settings navigation capability.
metadata.task_rationale: Leverages model's demonstrated ability to navigate Chrome settings. Privacy settings require similar navigation skills (Settings sidebar) but involves a toggle switch instead of radio buttons.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome Settings > Privacy and security and enabling the 'Send a Do Not Track request' toggle. Evaluator uses official enable_do_not_track getter with custom metric checking string or boolean true. [Fixed: metric now handles string return type from getter]
fix_history: Fix 1: Metric check_do_not_track now handles string return type from get_enable_do_not_track getter (was only checking isinstance(result, bool), now also handles isinstance(result, str) by comparing result.lower() == 'true')

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_enable_do_not_track correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and returns 'true'/'false' string for the enable_do_not_track setting.
Metric correctly handles both string and bool return types: isinstance(result, str) branch converts to bool via result.lower() == 'true' and compares against expected_enabled.
Expected parameter handling is correct: with type='rule', metric receives {'expected_enabled': true} directly and accesses it via expected.get('expected_enabled', True).
Single-requirement instruction (enable Do Not Track) is fully covered by the single getter+metric pair.
Postconfig sleep(2) provides time for Chrome to flush Preferences to disk before getter reads it.
